articles.image_title: Klimawandel: TOPSHOT - An aerial photograph taken on November 13, 2025 shows a view of the Skirlington Coast holiday park, located on the North sea coast in an area which is experiencing intense coastal erosion, near Hornsea, in the East Riding of Yorkshire, north eastern England. The Holderness coastline, covering 61km between the Spurn nature reserve in the south and Flamborough in the north, experiences one of the fastest rates of erosion in Europe. The Holderness cliffs are eroding at average rate of around 1.5 metres per year, although individual cliff losses can exceed 20 metres per year. Over the last 1000 years, the coast has retreated by around 2 kilometres, resulting in the destruction of 26 villages listed in the Domesday survey of 1086. (Photo by Oli SCARFF / AFP via Getty Images)

articles.image_title: Treibhausgasemissionen: TOPSHOT - Workers dry coal pebbles at Grace International's green coal production site in N'Djamena, Chad, on April 30, 2025. Under the scorching sun of Chad, a country threatened by desertification, about twenty workers zigzag from one machine to another on the production site of so-called "ecological" charcoal, in Pont Belile, north of N'Djamena. The produced charcoal comes from unexploited plant waste: millet stems, sesame stems, or palm fronds. The carbonized residues are crushed and then mixed with a maceration of gum arabic to facilitate ignition, and clay to slow down combustion.
